cluster_summary: Multiple endpoints and data publications fail to verify that users have appropriate access to the requested resources. This includes missing validation of parent-child resource relationships, using incorrect permission levels, lacking authentication on sensitive data endpoints, failing to project out sensitive fields, trusting client-supplied identifiers for ownership, stale authorization caches, user-supplied projection bypass, and unvalidated webhook URLs leading to SSRF.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled webhook URLs, callback URLs, endpoint parameters, or request destinations into outbound HTTP clients, URL.openConnection, fetch helpers, proxy clients, or webhook dispatchers. Report code paths where scheme, host, redirect target, DNS resolution, and private-address ranges are not constrained before the outbound request. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 2 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should enforce scheme and host allowlists, block private and metadata addresses after DNS resolution, and validate redirect targets.

mechanism.missing_guard: scheme, host, redirect target, DNS resolution, and private-address ranges are not constrained before the outbound request
mechanism.name: attacker-controlled webhook or callback URL fetch
mechanism.sink_shape: outbound HTTP clients, URL.openConnection, fetch helpers, proxy clients, or webhook dispatchers
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled webhook URLs, callback URLs, endpoint parameters, or request destinations
mechanism.typical_fix: enforce scheme and host allowlists, block private and metadata addresses after DNS resolution, and validate redirect targets

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Replace the authorization check with a function that enforces the correct permission level (e.g., write permission instead of read permission, admin role instead of member role, or respect global configuration constraints).
sub_patterns.name: Missing permission level checks
sub_patterns.root_cause: Code uses a lower privilege level check (read access or membership) instead of the required higher privilege (write access or admin role).

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Validate URL to allow only http/https and reject private/loopback addresses; also enforce appropriate authorization for integration management.
sub_patterns.name: Server-side request forgery due to unvalidated webhook URL
sub_patterns.root_cause: User-supplied URL is used for outbound HTTP requests without validating scheme and host, allowing requests to internal addresses.
